extracted.intended_audience: ABC journalists, content makers, editors and producers (ABC staff and contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Official ABC editorial policies and guidance setting enforceable standards and interpretive guidance for producing and publishing ABC content, including news and broadcast material. Covers principles such as objectivity, harm/offence, and fair opportunity to respond, plus structural documents and explanatory guidance notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Policies (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Policies that set out the guiding principles of our editorial approach and the enforceable standards you must follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central set of policies for ABC content; it defines the guiding principles and the enforceable standards staff must follow when producing material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preamble that sets out the overriding aims and principles behind the Editorial Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the fundamental aims and principles which inform interpretation and application of the policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on Interpretation and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A Note on Interpretation and Scope of the editorial policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides directions on how to interpret the policies and clarifies the scope of their application across ABC content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance Notes that explain in more detail how to interpret and apply those standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary explanatory material offering practical interpretation and application advice for the enforceable standards in the policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Practice and Associated Standard for Television Program Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also access the ABC’s Code of Practice and Associated Standard for Television Program Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to related mandatory documents that further regulate broadcasting practice and program classification; these form part of the regulatory framework staff must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The ABC has a requirement set out in the ABC Act to 'ensure that the gathering and presentation … of news and information is accurate and impartial according to the recognised standards of objective journalism'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be gathered and presented accurately and impartially, meeting recognised standards of objective journalism as required by the ABC Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm and offence
rubrics_metrics.description: This guidance aims to help content makers think through the issues relating to Harm and offence and make informed decisions that uphold the standards while still enabling us to broadcast and publish risky and innovative content consistent with our…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is provided to help producers assess potential harm and offence, balance editorial aims with audience protection, and make reasoned decisions that uphold standards while allowing permissible risky or innovative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of this guidance note is on the provision of a fair opportunity to respond prior to disclosure of allegations and includes information for when allegations are made during live content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires giving a fair opportunity to respond before allegations are disclosed; includes special procedures and considerations for handling allegations that arise during live broadcasts.
